7.1: The Hebrew names each of the seven peoples with a singular collective noun; BSB uses plural names.

7.8: The Hebrew explicitly names the LORD twice; BSB uses “He” for the second occurrence.
7.9: The Hebrew joins “the covenant” and “the loving devotion” with “and”; BSB combines them as “His covenant of loving devotion.”
7.10: The Hebrew initially refers to the haters in the plural but to the recipient’s face and destruction in the singular; BSB initially uses plural “their faces.”
7.11: The Hebrew has singular “the commandment”; BSB has plural “the commandments.”
7.12: The Hebrew separately says to listen, keep, and do the ordinances; BSB says to listen and “keep them carefully.”
7.13: The Hebrew repeats “fruit” for the womb and the ground; BSB uses “fruit” and then “produce.”
7.15: The Hebrew calls these “the evil diseases of Egypt”; BSB expresses this as diseases “you knew in Egypt.”
7.16: The Hebrew says to “eat” the peoples and that your “eye” must not pity them; BSB says “destroy” and “Do not look on them with pity.”
7.17: The Hebrew uses singular “me” and “I” in the quoted question; BSB uses plural “we.”
7.19: The Hebrew explicitly says “your eyes saw”; BSB says “you saw.”
7.20: The Hebrew joins “the remaining” and “the hidden” with “and”; BSB combines them as “the survivors hiding from you.”
7.22: The Hebrew says “you cannot” and uses singular collective “the beast of the field”; BSB says “will not be enabled” and uses plural “wild animals.”
7.23: The Hebrew repeats the confusion root in a verb and noun; BSB expresses this as “throw them into great confusion.”
7.24: The Hebrew has singular “their name” and explicitly names “your hand”; BSB has plural “their names” and uses the verb “hand ... over.” The Hebrew links the final destruction with “until,” while BSB gives it as a separate statement.
7.25: The Hebrew explicitly says “in the fire” and uses singular “for yourself”; BSB says “burn up” and plural “for yourselves.”

33.4: The Hebrew says Moses “commanded” the law; BSB says he “gave” it.
33.5: The Hebrew does not explicitly name the king’s subject here; BSB supplies “the LORD.”
33.6: The Hebrew’s final clause has no explicit negative word; BSB introduces it with “nor.”
33.8: The Hebrew joins both Thummim and Urim to “Your godly man” without an explicit giving verb; BSB supplies “Give” and assigns the Thummim explicitly “to Levi.”
33.9: The Hebrew says “I have not seen him” in the singular and then uses plural verbs for keeping the word and covenant; BSB has “them” and then singular “he.”
33.10: The Hebrew uses plural verbs for teaching and setting incense, places incense in God’s nostrils, and has singular “whole offering”; BSB uses “He,” “before You,” and plural “whole burnt offerings.”
33.12: The Hebrew says “between his shoulders” without explicitly naming God in the shielding clause; BSB says “upon His shoulders” and supplies “God.”
33.14: The Hebrew names “moons” or months; BSB says “the seasons.”
33.15: The Hebrew names the “head” or summit of the ancient mountains; BSB says “the best” of them.
33.16: The Hebrew names “the bush” without an explicit word “burning”; BSB supplies “burning.”
33.17: The Hebrew gives the bull and wild-ox horns as direct nominal descriptions; BSB marks both comparisons with “like.”
33.18: The Hebrew has singular “your going out”; BSB uses plural “your journeys.”
33.19: The Hebrew says they will “suck” the abundance of the seas and repeats the sacrificing root in verb and noun; BSB has “feast on” and “offer sacrifices.”
33.20: The Hebrew joins the arm and head with “also”; BSB uses “or.” BSB also supplies “the domain of” before Gad.
33.21: The Hebrew ends with “with Israel”; BSB says “for Israel.”
33.23: The Hebrew addresses Naphtali directly with a singular command to inherit; BSB says “he shall take possession.”
33.25: The Hebrew does not explicitly name a gate; BSB supplies “of your gate.”
33.27: The Hebrew gives the command “Destroy” without an explicit object; BSB supplies “him.”
33.28: The Hebrew says “alone” and “his heavens”; BSB has “untroubled” and “the heavens.”

34.2: The Hebrew calls the sea “the rear sea”; BSB says “the Western Sea.”
34.4: The Hebrew uses the image of “your seed”; BSB says “your descendants.”
34.5: The Hebrew says “by the mouth of the LORD”; BSB says “as the LORD had said.”
34.6: The Hebrew names his burial or grave without a separate word “location”; BSB specifies “the location of his grave.”
34.7: The Hebrew has singular “his eye”; BSB has plural “his eyes.”
34.9: The Hebrew says Joshua was full of the spirit of wisdom; BSB has the passive “was filled.”
34.11: The Hebrew does not repeat “no prophet” or explicitly name Moses here; BSB supplies “no prophet” and names Moses as the one sent.
34.12: The Hebrew names “the strong hand” and “the great terror” and repeats “all”; BSB expands these to “mighty acts of power and awesome deeds” and supplies “no prophet.”

5.1: The Hebrew says “in your ears”; BSB says “in your hearing.”
5.2: The Hebrew uses the image of cutting the covenant; BSB says “made a covenant.”
5.3: The Hebrew explicitly names the LORD and uses “cut” for the covenant; BSB uses “He” and “make.”
5.5: The Hebrew ends with “saying” without an explicit subject there; BSB gives “And He said.” The Hebrew says the people did not go up the mountain; BSB says they “would not” go up.
5.7: The Hebrew explicitly names “My face”; BSB expresses the phrase as “before Me.”
5.8: The Hebrew names a carved image and explicitly places the waters “under the earth”; BSB says “an idol” and leaves the earth implicit in “the waters beneath.”
5.10: The Hebrew has plural “thousands” without an explicit noun “generations”; BSB has “a thousand generations.”
5.11: The Hebrew uses the image of lifting or bearing the name; BSB says “take the name.”
5.18: The Hebrew begins with “And”; BSB omits this conjunction.
5.19: The Hebrew begins with “And”; BSB omits this conjunction.
5.20: The Hebrew begins with “And”; BSB omits this conjunction.
5.21: The Hebrew uses different verbs for coveting the wife and desiring the house; BSB uses “covet” in both commands.
5.22: The Hebrew says “these words”; BSB says “these commandments.”
5.24: The Hebrew says God speaks with a human and that person lives; BSB recasts this as a person being able to live “even if” God speaks with him.
5.28: The Hebrew twice names “the voice of the words” and explicitly names the LORD twice; BSB has “the words” and uses “He” for the second divine name.
5.30: The Hebrew explicitly says to return “for yourselves”; BSB simply says “Return.”
5.31: The Hebrew uses singular “the whole commandment”; BSB has plural “all the commandments.”
5.33: The Hebrew uses singular “all the way”; BSB has plural “all the ways.”

6.1: The Hebrew begins with singular “the commandment” and does not explicitly name the person commanded to teach; BSB has plural “the commandments” and supplies “me.”
6.2: The Hebrew has singular “your son” and “your son’s son”; BSB has plural “your children and grandchildren.”
6.6: The Hebrew has singular “your heart”; BSB has plural “your hearts.”
6.7: The Hebrew uses a verb whose literal image is sharpening the words for the children; BSB expresses this as teaching them diligently.
6.8: The Hebrew has singular “a sign” and “your hand,” and places the frontlets “between your eyes”; BSB has plural “reminders,” “hands,” and “on your foreheads.”
6.9: The Hebrew has singular “your house”; BSB has plural “your houses.”
6.11: The Hebrew names hewn cisterns and repeats the hewing root; BSB says “wells that you did not dig.”
6.13: The Hebrew says to serve Him without an explicit word “only”; BSB supplies “only.”
6.17: The Hebrew explicitly says He “commanded” these things; BSB says He “has given” them.
6.18: The Hebrew says “in the eyes of the LORD” and ends with “the LORD” without “your God” or an explicit “to give”; BSB has “in the sight of the LORD” and supplies “your God” and “to give” in the oath clause.

6.21: The Hebrew explicitly says “your son”; BSB uses “him.”
6.25: The Hebrew uses singular “this whole commandment”; BSB has plural “every one of these commandments.”
